text: The Railpower GG20B Green Goat is a low-emissions diesel hybrid switcher locomotive manufactured by Railpower Technologies Corp. It is powered by a single Caterpillar C9 six-cylinder inline engine producing 300 horsepower (224 kW), which is paired with a large battery bank, resulting in a combined total power output of 2,000 horsepower (1,490 kW). Since their first introduction in 2004, more than 50 GG20B diesel-electric hybrid switchers have been produced. BNSF Railway and Vehicle Projects converted one GG20B into an experimental hydrogen fuel cell locomotive, designated HH20B. This locomotive was first publicly demonstrated on June 29, 2009, in Topeka, Kansas. The locomotive, originally built in 1957 as Canadian Pacific 8637 (renumbered 1544 in the 1980s), was a GMD GP9 locomotive. In 2006, it was rebuilt into a GG20B for Canadian Pacific but was not delivered due to the cancellation of the order. It was sold to BNSF in 2008 and shipped to BNSF's shops in Topeka, Kansas, where the diesel generator set was removed and a fuel cell power unit installed in its place. Hydrogen storage is provided by a set of tanks located in a heavily vented enclosure on top of the locomotive's long hood, above the batteries. To date, this locomotive is the largest land vehicle on Earth powered exclusively by hydrogen fuel cells. In 2023, the locomotive, without its hydrogen components, was donated to the Oklahoma Railroad Museum, where it is planned to be used as a control car and for electricity generation at the end of excursion trains.
